name: Quality Control & Inspection

objectives.text: Describe why food products are inspected before they are sold to families and stores
Identify quality characteristics of fresh fruits and vegetables using sight, touch, and smell, such as color, firmness, and aroma
Identify signs that a food product does not meet quality standards, such as bruising, discoloration, wilting, or damaged packaging
Compare food products sold under different grades, such as Grade AA and Grade A eggs, and explain what the grade tells a buyer
Explain the steps involved in inspecting a food product for defects from sampling to recording results
Measure and record quality attributes of a food sample using simple tools such as a scale, ruler, thermometer, and color chart
Summarize the purposes of quality assurance and food safety tests performed on food products during harvest, transport, and processing
Summarize the characteristics of USDA quality and yield grades for food products such as beef, eggs, and fresh produce
Apply quality control standards and a sampling plan to evaluate a batch of food products for defects
Distinguish mandatory federal safety inspection from voluntary quality grading of food products
Describe FSIS protocols for pre-mortem and post-mortem inspection of livestock and poultry
Conduct quality assurance tests on food products such as pH, Brix, moisture content, and sensory evaluation
Analyze factors that affect quality and yield grades, such as marbling, maturity, fat thickness, and ribeye area in beef carcasses
Examine the desirable qualities of food products from different classifications such as meats, dairy, eggs, and produce
Assign quality and yield grades to carcasses, retail cuts, or eggs according to industry standards as practiced in FFA Meats and Poultry Evaluation
Evaluate quality assurance test results using control charts and recommend corrective procedures when a process falls out of specification
Evaluate care and handling procedures during storage and distribution for their ability to maintain original food quality and yield
Evaluate the effectiveness of a quality control checkpoint in a food production process
Design a quality control inspection protocol for raw products or a specific food product line, including sampling, tests, acceptance criteria, and records
Create a grading and quality record-keeping plan for a product marketed through a supervised agricultural experience

changes: Kept and reworded all six existing objectives, attaching standards to the grade 9 and up items. Added early-grade sensory quality, grade comparison, and measurement skills. Added high school competencies for QA test purposes and conduct, USDA quality and yield grades, grading versus FSIS inspection, pre-mortem and post-mortem protocols, grade factors, product class qualities, FFA-style grading, control charts with corrective action, storage and distribution handling, and an SAE grading plan. Left pathogens, HACCP, and labeling to the sibling sub-topics.
